notes.framing: No quantum-advantage claim. Classical solvers are exact or near-exact on every instance; QAOA is reported for the formulation and hardware study.
notes.approx_ratio: optimum / objective of a feasible sample (minimisation, 1 = optimal)
notes.q_a:
Instance builders for Q-A (case scheduling) and Q-B (document set cover).

Everything is derived from packages/knowledge; nothing is sampled at random.

Q-A modelling choices (documented here and copied into results.json):
- Case steps: process steps of the bundle's benefits whose action needs a visit:
  ``office.resolve`` -> office visit (60 min), ``documents.checklist`` -> document submission or
  pickup (30 min), ``appointment.prepare`` -> appointment (60 min). Steps are taken round-robin
  over the bundle's benefits so consecutive steps sit at different offices.
- Place: the office from the benefit's ``office_rules`` for the persona facts. If that office has
  no parseable opening hours, the nearest office of the same carrier and region that has them is
  used (``substituted_for`` records it). Steps without a usable place are listed as skipped.
- Slots: weekdays from Monday, candidate starts on a fixed grid (default 08:00, 09:00, 10:00,
  11:00, 13:00, 14:00); a start is allowed only if [start, start + duration) lies inside an
  opening interval.
- Deadlines: no process step in the knowledge base defines a deadline (the process files state
  that reminders are prompts, not statutory deadlines). We use the reminder ``after_days`` as a
  soft due day where present and the horizon end otherwise.
- Travel: straight-line distance between the postcode centroids (GeoNames, data/postcodes-at.json)
  at 30 km/h, rounded to minutes. Vienna postcodes share one centroid in that file, so most
  intra-Vienna travel times are 0; the Lower Austria persona has real distances.

Q-B: elements are a bundle's documents[] entries (required ones by default); sets are the
sources a person would visit or contact (employer, pension carrier, doctor, ...), matched from the
``obtain_from`` text with fixed patterns. An element belongs to every source its text names.
notes.qubo:
QUBO formulations (lotse-rl.md §9) and bitstring decoding.

A QUBO is an upper-triangular matrix Q (diagonal = linear terms) plus an offset;
E(x) = sum_{k<=l} Q[k, w] x_k x_l + offset for x in {0,1}^n.

Q-A (case scheduling), x_{i,t} = 1 if step i starts in allowed slot t:
  H = A sum_i (sum_t x_{i,t} - 1)^2
    + B sum_{overlapping (i,t),(j,u), i != j} x_{i,t} x_{j,u}
    + sum_{i,t} lateness_i(t) x_{i,t}
    + C sum_{consecutive (i,t)->(j,u)} tau(i,j) x_{i,t} x_{j,u}
  with C = 1 (travel minutes and lateness share one unit) and
  A = B = 1 + max_k (lateness_k + sum_l C tau_kl [k,w consecutive]), i.e. larger than anything a
  single variable can gain on the objective terms. For every instance we enumerate (n <= 20) or
  anneal and check that the QUBO ground state is feasible and equals the CP-SAT optimum.
  "Overlapping" = same day and intersecting [start, end); "consecutive" = same day, (j,u) starts
  at or after the end of (i,t) and no grid start lies in between.

Q-B (minimum set cover, Lucas 2014 §5.1), x_i = 1 if set i is used, y_{a,m} = 1 if element a is
covered exactly m times (m = 1..M_a, M_a = number of sets containing a):
  H = A sum_a (1 - sum_m y_{a,m})^2 + A sum_a (sum_m m y_{a,m} - sum_{i: a in V_i} x_i)^2
    + B sum_i x_i,   with B = 1 and A = 2 (Lucas requires 0 < B < A).
  Decoding reads only the set bits; a sample is feasible if the chosen sets cover every element.
notes.qaoa:
QAOA and warm-start QAOA: parameter training on an exact numpy statevector (n <= 20),
Qiskit circuits for sampling on Aer or IBM hardware.

Energies are divided by the largest absolute QUBO coefficient before building the circuit so
that angles are comparable across instances. Plain QAOA starts in |+>^n with the RX mixer.
Warm-start QAOA (Egger, Marecek, Woerner 2021) starts in prod_k RY(theta_k)|0> with
sin^2(theta_k/2) = c_k, c_k = eps or 1 - eps from the CP-SAT bits (eps = 0.25), and uses the
mixer RY(theta_k) RZ(-2 beta) RY(-theta_k). Warm-starting from the exact optimum is the most
favourable case for QAOA by construction; we report it as such, not as an independent solver.
notes.git_sha: aer.git_sha / hardware.git_sha are the commits whose code produced each block (recorded after rebasing onto main; the ml/quantum tree there differs from the top-level git_sha only in run metadata).
notes.hardware: IBM Heron (ibm_marrakesh) via qiskit-ibm-runtime SamplerV2, p=1, 4096 shots, optimization_level=3 transpilation; QAOA angles trained on the exact statevector. Hardware results are noisy and are reported for reproducibility, not as evidence of advantage.
